title: Chapter 183: Return
html:
“Calm down!” Chen Ge immediately ran to the middle of the corridor. “We’re all allies here; there’s no need to harm each other!”

Trapped between two Red Specters, Chen Ge’s back was drenched in sweat. The absurdity of the situation shocked even him: two Red Specters stood ready to fight, while he, a living human, tried to mediate. Perhaps because of his intervention, neither the boy nor Zhang Ya attacked.

In truth, the boy had already compromised. Since waking, he had steadily absorbed the Third Sick Hall’s blood vessels. The longer the standoff lasted, the stronger he became.

“You may have his body, but I’m keeping the head.” The boy shared a unique bond with the Third Sick Hall. If the building itself was a monster, he was its child, granting him perfect control over much of what existed there.

Countless blood vessels surfaced along the corridor and coiled around the old man’s neck. Having resigned himself to his fate, he suddenly opened his eyes and began to struggle. Zhang Ya’s foot still pinned him down, leaving him unable to move.

The vessels bored into his neck, and what followed was gruesome. His screams reverberated through the hall as the vessels formed tentacles and carried his severed head to the boy.

“What kind of mistake has the old man made?” Chen Ge was past feeling pity for the man. After all, he did try to kill him earlier.

“When the door first opened, he used the patients as test subjects.” The boy’s hollow gaze settled on the head in his arms. “He forced them through, including my mother.

Hugging the old man’s head, the boy smiled sweetly. “He is a selfish hypocrite. I fell asleep because of him and several of his patients.”

“Several patients? There are other people behind the door?” Chen Ge edged closer to Zhang Ya, where he felt safer.

“I promised Doctor Chen that I would guard the door after entering. Five years ago, however, someone forced it open from outside.” The boy began recounting what had happened. “The old man had cancer and knew he did not have long to live. Hoping to extend his life, he turned his attention to the world behind the door.

“But he was afraid, so just as he had many years earlier, he sent several patients through first. The Third Sick Hall was an isolation ward, and its patients had neither family nor social connections. It was easy to keep the entire procedure secret.

“After a week of experiments convinced him there was no danger, the director entered with several patients.” Still smiling, the boy stroked the old man’s screaming head. “Once the door closed, this became my world. Nothing inside the Third Sick Hall could harm me.

“I never intended to hurt them. After so many years of boredom, I only wanted something to do. To my surprise, they opened the door and allowed monsters into the Third Sick Hall so they could escape. Some even let the creatures possess them.

“By the time I discovered their plan, it was too late. They imprisoned me in the electroconvulsive-therapy room and left the dying director to watch over me while the others escaped, carrying their sin and terror with them.”

Chen Ge nodded. “I’ve encountered several Third Sick Hall patients in the real world. Each was possessed by a lanky monster. The old man said those creatures embodied human desire.”

“They did originate behind the door, but they are also the weakest creatures here.” The statement chilled Chen Ge. He had always assumed the mirror monster occupied that position.

“Seven patients entered five years ago, and the weakest monsters possessed four of them. I couldn’t identify what happened to the remaining three.” The boy glanced at Chen Ge. “If you’ve reached this place, you must already have fought them. The others may come looking for you.”

“Can you tell me about the three that are most dangerous?”

“An extraordinarily beautiful woman, a man with a ruined face, and one called Wu Fei.” The boy ground his teeth over the last name. “Wu Fei devised the plan to imprison me.”

Then he added, “But Wu Fei isn’t the hardest to deal with. Beware the man with the ruined face. He is the most dangerous.”

“Thank you for the reminder.”

“Don’t thank me yet. I have a favor to ask.” After studying Chen Ge for a long moment, the boy finally revealed his purpose. “I am only a personality, and the Third Sick Hall behind the door is my host. I have been here so long that, in a sense, my consciousness has merged with the building. Outsiders cannot kill me. They can only weaken me and force me to sleep.

“But they can influence me by harming my second personality. They might even control me through him. That is my greatest concern. If the need arises, please protect him. I have no family left in that world, and he is my only friend.”

“Of course. Your second personality is my friend too, so I would never refuse to help him.” Chen Ge hoped to befriend the boy—and perhaps one day recruit him. The Haunted House needed someone his age.

“I hope you keep that promise.” Carrying the old man’s head, the boy returned to Room 3. “Remaining here too long will damage both mind and body. Negative thoughts will fill you, and eventually, you will go mad.”

He opened Room 3 and placed the old man’s head beside the bed. “I’ll send you back. If you encounter trouble, come here at midnight. I can hold the door open for one minute.”

“Why one minute?” Chen Ge’s eyes twitched.

“That’s the limit of my control,” the boy replied. “This world is vast, and it contains many doors. Some, like this one, have guardians; others stand unattended. A guarded door normally remains open for one minute.”

“Okay, I understand.” Chen Ge lowered his head, thinking about the door in his Haunted House.

When both Chen Ge and Zhang Ya walked into Room 3, the boy closed the door. He stood beside the door. “You can go back now.”

“But how?”

The boy pointed at the door of Room 3. “Push it open, you only have one minute.”
